key_findings.claim: Voc Loss in p-type c-Si (Field Measurements)
key_findings.detail:
Real-world field data from a 2-year grid-connected plant (Wang et al., 2018):

| Module | Pmax Loss | Voc Loss | Isc Loss | FF Loss |
|--------|----------|---------|---------|--------|
| Module 1 (mild PID) | −3.00% | −0.29% | −1.40% | −1.97% |
| Module 2 (moderate PID) | −21.90% | −10.00% | −1.75% | −19.82% |
| Module 3 (severe PID) | −48.67% | −30.31% | −1.75% | −26.95% |

**Pattern:** Voc and FF losses dominate; Isc loss is minor (~1–2%) in p-type c-Si.
- [[papers/Elsevier-498-3124-2-s2.0-85033564380-2018-J-Performance variation of dark current density voltage characteristics for PID affected monocrystalli.pdf#page=3|Wang et al. (2018), p.3]]

key_findings.claim: Voc Loss in Laboratory Accelerated Testing (p-type multi-c-Si)
key_findings.detail:
At cell level, −1000 V, 85°C:
- After 1.5 h: Voc drops from **0.61 V to 0.30 V** (51% reduction)
- After 2.5 h: Voc drops to **0.12 V** (80% reduction)
- [[papers/Elsevier-541-3483-2-s2.0-84991699729-2016-J-Microscopic aspects of potential induced degradation phenomena and their recovery processes for p ty.pdf#page=3|Luo et al. (2016), p.3]]

The recombination current density ($J_R$) in the depletion region increases with Na⁺ concentration:

- $V_{oc} \propto \ln(J_{ph} / J_R)$; as $J_R$ increases, $V_{oc}$ decreases
- At $1.0 \times 10^{16}$ cm$^{-3}$ metal ion concentration: minority carrier lifetime drops from $2.18 \times 10^{-6}$ s to $1.0 \times 10^{-8}$ s → $V_{oc}$ drops from 0.640 V to 0.337 V (~47% reduction)
- [[papers/Elsevier-498-3124-2-s2.0-85033564380-2018-J-Performance variation of dark current density voltage characteristics for PID affected monocrystalli.pdf#page=4|Wang et al. (2018), p.4]]

Voc degradation is most severe in substrings at the module edges (highest negative bias):

- **Substring 1 (near frame):** Voc −38.50%
- **Substring 2 (center):** Voc −8.97%
- **Substring 3 (near frame):** Voc −44.30%

- [[papers/Elsevier-498-3124-2-s2.0-85033564380-2018-J-Performance variation of dark current density voltage characteristics for PID affected monocrystalli.pdf#page=5|Wang et al. (2018), p.5]]

CIGS PID preferentially reduces Voc as the primary loss mechanism (unlike FF-dominated c-Si PID):

- $V_{oc}$ drops first and most severely as cation accumulation at the CIGS/CdS junction reduces the built-in voltage $V_{bi}$
- Isc is relatively preserved until late-stage complete failure
- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=3|Theelen et al. (2018), p.3]]

Rear-side PID-polarization produces substantial Voc loss from increased surface recombination:

- Rear-side Voc loss: **28–36%** after 136 h of PID stress
- Front-side Voc loss: 17–20% (lower than rear, which suffers complete AlOx charge neutralization)
- [[papers/Elsevier-424-2622-2-s2.0-85065845673-2019-J-Physics of potential induced degradation in bifacial p PERC solar cells.pdf#page=3|Chen et al. (2019), p.3]]

key_findings.claim: TOPCon: Significant Voc Loss Under Dark Stress
key_findings.detail:
TOPCon PID-polarization under dark accelerated conditions:
- Voc loss: **11.1%** (at 96 h, −1000 V, 60°C, dark)
- Recovers rapidly under illumination (photoconductivity of SiNx dissipates accumulated charge)
- Under field-realistic conditions with 0.1-sun UV: Voc loss is much smaller (~few percent)
- [[papers/Wiley-105-888-2-s2.0-85183130481-2024-J-Field-representative evaluation of PID-polarization in TOPCon PV modules by accelerated stress testi.pdf#page=4|Luo et al. (2024), p.4]]

key_findings.claim: Perovskite: Voc Stability Is a Diagnostic Marker
key_findings.detail:
In perovskite polarization-type PID (PID-p), Voc **remains stable** even as Jsc and FF collapse:

- Stage 1 (0–20 h): Voc stable; Jsc 24.14 → 18.41 mA/cm²; FF 81.09% → 71.89%
- Stage 2 (20–100 h): Voc still stable; Jsc → 15.22 mA/cm²; FF → 26.86%
- Voc stability distinguishes polarization-type from shunting-type PID in perovskites
- [[papers/Wiley-45-301-2-s2.0-105008480848-2025-J-Failure Analysis of Polarization-Type Potential-Induced Degradation of Perovskite Solar Cells.pdf#page=5|Li et al. (2025), p.5]]
